newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. food agency to aid drought victims in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: U.N. food agency to aid drought victims in Kenya.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Tuesday it would shortly start providing drought -hit northeastern and eastern Kenya with food aid for 477,000 stricken people.

A WFP statement said the $12.3 million emergency operation would last for six months in Northeastern and Eastern Provinces, where the failure of three consecutive rainy seasons were seriously affecting people.
President Daniel arap Moi a week ago declared a national famine disaster in Kenya and scrapped taxes on imported food for victims. He appealed to international organisations for help.
WFP said 17,848 tonnes of food would be provided to an estimated 207,000 people in the drought-stricken areas of Garissa, Mandera, Wajir, Isiolo and Marsabit in Northeastern Province.
The remaining 6,846 tonnes of food would be given to 270,000 schoolchildren primarily in Eastern Province, bringing the total number of children receiving a free lunch to 480,000.
A ship loaded with 3,600 tonnes of beans for WFP programmes in Kenya is expected to arrive in Mombasa port on February 10.
Another ship with 20,000 tonnes of maize meal, pulses and sorghum donated by the United States for WFP's operations in Kenya, south Sudan and the Great Lakes region arrives on February 15.
